memos.Sleepover notes:
"How long was your Sleepover
One night so far

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Affectionate
Velcro Dog
Trusting

What made you smile or laugh about them?
Jo Lee is so sweet. She’s loves to cuddle up against someone any chance she can.

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
She’s a delight! But she’s got some puppy tendencies to grow out of, like: she likes to chew and she’s not quite potty trained. She slept in a crate all night but she whined for about 20 minutes before settling in. And she’s a classic Velcro dog - never wants to leave your side.

Where did the dog sleep
Crate

How was the dog in the car?
Relaxed
Anxious and restless

How was the dog when left alone?
Some whining or pacing

What is their housetraining status?
In progress / working on it: Needs very frequent potty breaks and close supervision. Has multiple accidents per day, but goes outside once in a while.

How did the dog do in the bath?
Tolerant

How did they do with other adults in the home or visitors? Did they meet visitors, or only hang with you?
Loved everyone

How did they do with cats or small animals (if present)?
Not applicable

How did they do with children (if present)?
No children present

How did they do with other dogs (if present)?
Loved them

How would you describe their energy level?
Moderate

How were they on leash?
Pulled sometimes

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
We’re definitely thinking about it! But we’ve only had her since yesterday afternoon."

memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

animals.name: Little Dude
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Hi, I'm Little Dude! I'm a year-old Golden Retriever/Lab mix and I recently had a sleepover with a foster family, and had the time of my life. 🎾

I met three resident dogs on my very first day and didn't miss a beat — no drama, just wagging tails. Turns out I really thrive with canine company, so a home with another dog (or a dog park bestie) would make me even happier.

I'm already fully housebroken and slept through my first night in a crate without a peep — I know how to settle in and behave. During the day I keep myself busy with toys, and I'll happily fetch a ball and bring it right back for another throw.

I've got medium-to-high energy, but don't worry — I chill out easily and I'm calm and relaxed once we're inside. A yard would be my dream come true, though, since I love to zip around and burn off steam outside.

I'm looking for a family who'll toss the ball with me, maybe bring home a canine sibling, and give me a little yard space to run laps in. Think that could be you?

Adoption fee includes spay/neuter, vaccinations, microchip, and lifetime behavior support from Austin Pets Alive!

animals.name: Sandy (Cosmic Cocoa)
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Snuggly, Courageous, Loving

Sandy aka Cosmic Cocoa is a total cuddle bug who just wants to be wherever her people are. She settled into her foster home almost immediately and was quick to start purring and soaking up all the pets. She especially loves cheek scratches, and if you stop petting her too soon, she'll gently rub against you to ask for more

With a low-key energy level, Sandy would much rather spend her day snuggled up beside you than chasing toys. She gets along well with other cats but would prefer a home without dogs, as they make her nervous. While she hasn't been around children in foster care, her gentle personality suggests she'd likely do well with respectful kids. Sandy came to APA! after the Uvalde floods and has proven to be incredibly resilient, sweet, and trusting. If you're looking for a loving companion who never gets tired of cuddles, Sandy is your girl.

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Sandy (Cosmic Cocoa), please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

memos.Medical Consult:
Peppa was recently checked over and is not pregnant, which is good news. She is being treated for mild skin irritation with redness, dry skin, and small scabs, and is currently taking cephalexin (500 mg by mouth twice daily), fish oil (once daily), and cetirizine (30 mg by mouth once daily) through August 2, 2026; any needed medication refills should be discussed if her skin has not fully improved by then. Please provide an email update or recheck in about 14 days (around August 5, 2026) to let the medical team know how her skin is healing. Her outlook is good, though she may need additional treatment if the skin problems persist.

Please see the medical record for the complete medical history. This is only a synopsis of the most important information. 7/24/26 TH

memos.Disclaimer: Animal intaked during 2026 Central Texas flood
memos.Volunteer Notes:
How long was your Sleepover
1 week

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Affectionate
Velcro Dog
Cheerful

What made you smile or laugh about them?
It’s endearing how clingy she is! She follows me from room to room and loves to cuddle. When she gets really excited, her whole sways from the force of her tail wags.

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
She has pretty intense separation anxiety. At first, she’d even bark even when I closed the door to use the restroom. Over the course of just a week, she became more desensitized and no longer barked when I was out of her line of sight. I’d leave for work everyday and watch her through a doggy camera - she would bark and whine for 5-10 minutes immediately after I left, but napped on the couch all day until I came back home. I would leave the TV on for her but she’d seriously just sleep the entire time I was gone!

If you live in an apartment, the barking might be something you should keep in mind. I did not have a crate so she roamed freely. Never had any issues with using the restroom inside, messing up my furniture, or anything.

She LOVES (!!!!!!) sniffing walks. She’s the type of dog that stops and sniffs every bush. Would tug when she saw another dog because she got excited, but stopped if I said “noooooo.” Super curious about everything!

I did notice that she’s scared of a lot of things (like doors) but became more confident in such a short period of time. Has the typical chihuahua shakes. Would periodically wheeze/cough a lot. Do keep in mind that she does not go up/down stairs so you have to carry her. She’s less than 10 lbs, really not a big deal.

Where did the dog sleep
Dog Bed

How was the dog in the car?
Some whining or pacing, but settled

How was the dog when left alone?
Barking
Some whining or pacing

What is their housetraining status?
Fully housetrained - Consistently holds it when left alone, and gives clear signals when they need to go outside. May have had accidents in the first couple days, but leveled out completely once the dog learned the routines.

How did the dog do in the bath?
Seemed nervous or anxious
Tolerant

How did they do with other adults in the home or visitors? Did they meet visitors, or only hang with you?
Loved everyone

How did they do with cats or small animals (if present)?
Not applicable

How did they do with children (if present)?
No children present

How did they do with other dogs (if present)?
No other dogs present

If you select 'Not Recommended" to any of the answers above. Please use this space to tell us why you choice that selection.

How would you describe their energy level?
Low

How were they on leash?
Pulled constantly

Do you want to add any details about the information you provided above?

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
YES. I am in and out of town too often to be caring for an animal, but if I was settled somewhere and could afford dog boarding I would absolutely adopt her. She is a true sweetheart and is extremely loving!!!! I was concerned with her separation anxiety at first, but it’s gotten so much better in just a week. I’m sure if you have her longer she would be much more desensitized. She is very well behaved and understands the word “no”

memos.Behavior Team FFU:
from foster: High Energy, Jumping, Biting: She gets easily excited and jumps up on people/furniture and sometimes start biting at hands, ankles, and occasionally jumping up at our face. It's not constant, but when it happens, we have a hard time controlling it; she is very strong. We try just ignoring until she sits and calms down, but this behavior seems to be getting worse as she gets more comfortable here, so I was wondering if there's anything else we can try doing to train her to not jump/bite in these moments.
Whining, Crate Training: We are trying to make sure she is okay alone. We have her in a separate room because we have a resident dog and she initially had ticks. We've slowly let her have more time outside of the room this week, but she always whines and paws at the door when put back in the room or whenever she hears us outside. She will eventually sleep and is fine sleeping through the night in the room, but we got a crate to start crate training her. In the room, she will go in the crate herself and sleep in it. She will sometimes try to jump on the crate when bored, but otherwise has not damaged anything in that room or had any accidents. Should we continue keeping the crate, opened in her room, or should we crate train outside of the room and eventually transition her to sleep and rest there (i.e. somewhere in our living room)? Also, is there anything more we can do to have her be more comfortable in the room when she's awake to stop her from whining and scratching at the door?
Resident Dog Interaction: We recently introduced her to our resident dog (she's 1 years old and he's 5 years old). They are fine together on walks, but when they are at home, they constantly play/fight. We have to keep them in separate rooms in order for them to rest. Is this okay or is there more we should be doing to get them to the point where they can be in the same room and rest when they're tired?
sent resources addressing each point. asked for profile updates as well.

7/26 foster asked for clarification around a good routine of forcing charlotte to take a break when playing. she rests in her crate during the day and gets to hang out in the evening. foster thinks play between dogs is mostly mutual asked about keeping her from jumping over the back of the couch or jumping from chair to couch or walking on the coffee table. suggested taking away all furniture privileges until she gets the idea, then adding the couch back in. sent tie down resources. Jess

animals.name: Quilligan
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Those glowing, liquid-amber eyes look straight into your soul while a tiny splash of white paint runs right down the middle of a chocolate-brown nose. Quilligan is a friendly, social dog who wags her tail to say hello to every person and dog that walks past her. This smart girl balances a love for playtime with a calm ability to sit quietly on the couch with you for hours. She is relaxed in the car, sleeps in her crate, and is fully house-trained. Visitors receive a warm, affectionate welcome from this well-behaved companion, though she shows a bit of nervousness when it is time for a bath.

Quilligan is waiting for you to welcome them home.

animals.name: Ol Lady
animals.kennelCardMemo:
If you are looking for a soft-hearted soul to fill your home with quiet love and companionship, Ol' Lady is ready to steal your heart. This senior boxer girl may have some miles on her, but she still knows how to make every single day special.

Personality: Ol' Lady is quite simply the sweetest, most gentle girl you will ever meet. She is a total people-lover who is happiest just hanging out by your side and soaking up affection.

Mobility: While her back legs don't work as well as they used to, Ol' Lady is a resilient trooper who can still get around just fine to greet her favorite humans.

Medical Care: She does have some ongoing health concerns, but our clinic team is fully committed to working side-by-side with her adopter to establish a comprehensive, supportive treatment plan.

If you have room in your heart and home for a seasoned sweetheart who just wants a comfortable place to rest her head and share her love, Ol' Lady is waiting for you.

She is currently located at our Elgin hub. If you would like to schedule a meet-and-greet or have questions, please email us at transporthub@austinpetsalive.org

Guarded-grave given geriatric dog with multiple severe medical issues including multiple mammary masses, possible pulmonary mass (primary vs metastasis), severe spondylosis, healed left hind limb fracture, severe mobility issues in the hind end, suspect kidney issues. Despite her many medical issues  she is a very sweet girl who is very eager to eat. We are hoping to find her a hospice foster who can love on her and give her pain meds and snacks, and monitor her quality of life closely. We have submitted some blood work and urine to the lab, once we get those results we may add in additional medications (NSAIDs) for comfort if her organs are able to tolerate them. We do not want her to suffer, and plan on humanely euthanizing her when her quality of life is declining.

memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

animals.name: Ozzie
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Hi! I'm Ozzie, your future bundle of joy! I'm all about fun and games, always ready for an adventure or a good play session. I'm smart and quick to learn, so we can master new tricks together. I walk nicely on a leash (bikes, cars, barking dogs, little kids on scooters, and strangers don’t phase me), making every stroll enjoyable. After a day of excitement, I'm happy to relax in my crate, dreaming of our next day together.

I’m a social butterfly and love everyone, bringing smiles and energy wherever I go. I love being active and can get pretty hyped up when excited, but I respond well to gentle corrections because I want to please my people. I'm still learning my name, but I do come when called. I would thrive in a household where both my mind and body are kept active.

If you're looking for a loyal friend with a silly side to share in all your adventures and cozy nights, I'm your guy. Let's make every moment count together!

I touched her shoulder and down her leg and she didn't wince or get scared, but she will not put all of her weight on her right leg.

She's pretty big in comparison, but Claudelie couldn't care less. She immediately started following Cookie around and mimicking what she does. She's gentle with our cats. Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?

memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

animals.name: Cartoonishly Masculine
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Loving, Curious, Content

Cartoonishly Masculine may have a larger-than-life name, but his personality is pure sweetheart. This big-hearted orange tabby has adorable tiger stripes, soulful green eyes, and a striped tail worthy of its own dramatic entrance. His slightly shorter front legs even give him a touch of Puss in Boots charm.

Most of all, Cartoonishly Masculine has enough affection to brighten every day. His favorite place is wherever you are, and he will happily cuddle, make biscuits, or purr beside you while you work, read, or relax. He does not demand constant attention; he is simply content to share your space and gaze at you with those wonderfully expressive green eyes. When he does speak, his tiny mew is an adorable surprise.

He has just the right amount of playful energy, too. Ribbon toys, little fish, toy mice, and watching the world through the window are all high on his list of favorite activities. Curious and easygoing, he is genuinely happy simply spending time with his people.

Cartoonishly Masculine is currently carrying a few extra pounds and would benefit from measured meals and regular playtime—something he will surely be enthusiastic about if it involves his favorite toys!

After a stressful rescue from a shelter affected by recent flooding, Cartoonishly Masculine settled into his foster home with remarkable ease, behaving as though he had lived there for years. He has responded warmly to every person he has met. His experience with dogs and children is unknown.
During his brief stay at the APA! cattery, he preferred having his own space around other cats, so any feline introductions should be slow and thoughtful.

If you’ve been hoping for a cat who simply loves being with you, Cartoonishly Masculine may be your perfect match. Whether you’re working from home or relaxing with a good book, he’ll be happiest purring nearby. Playful when the toys come out and peaceful when it’s time to settle in, this affectionate orange gentleman is genuinely delighted just to be part of your life.

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Cartoonishly Masculine, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

memos.Behavior Team FFU:
[Bite Incident] [RETURN] FTA emailed last night reporting "I am reaching out regarding an incident that happened this evening with Kamaya. My 18 month old son was trying to play with her toy and she gave several warning barks/snips but when he walked past her later, she bit him on the face. Then he was quite a while away walking and she lunged at him again. I’m unsure where to call or what to do but I’m nervous a more serious incident may occur as she gets more comfortable. She’s fine with my 3 year old but suddenly got defensive and aggressive with my 18 month old. Were surprised since she’s been beyond playful and calm since we met her. Please let me know what to do next."

Dog Support team replied initially advising that they keep Kamaya separated from the kids. I followed up this morning reiterating that they keep Kamaya and both kids separated until we know more. I sent bite questions and additional questions about the incident. Offered a phone call if that is easier. AKC

*UPDATE: Sleepover host replied providing more details about the bite incident to her 18 month old son. The bite did not break the skin, it left a small red mark that faded away completely with a little time. The female sleepover host was sitting on the couch and Kamaya was on the couch next to her with a toy. Their 18 month old son was standing on the ground with his hands on the couch. He was initially reaching towards the toy that Kamaya had and she first quickly covered the toy with her front paws and then gave a quick growl and air snap in his direction. The boy started to turn towards his mom and move towards her when Kamaya quickly lunged forward biting him on the cheek. It was a very fast nip and she just laid there afterwards. The mom picked up her son and was checking him. A minute later the boy was set back on the ground and tried to walk past Kamaya who was still on the couch but was no longer actively playing with the toy. As the boy passed she again tried to lunge towards him but no contact was made. The male sleepover host came over and put Kamaya in the crate and they kept her separated from the kids after that. The female sleepover host said that the next day while Kamaya was crate the boys (18 month old and 3 yr old) were walking near the crate and Kamaya low growled briefly. Prior to that she had no negative reactions around the 3 yr old.

I spoke in person with the male sleepover host when he physically returned Kamaya. He had been sitting at the dining table facing the living room when the incident happened. He said that he didn't feel uncomfortable with Kamaya's behavior leading up to the bite and that he was willing to keep working with her but his wife was too nervous and not comfortable trying to make it work. I'm choosing not to add a resource guarding (RG) attribute at this time because there is not enough evidence to support that RG was the reason for Kamaya's reaction. It is possible she was not as comfortable with the youngest child. Adding a BC and child score 3 to indicate that slightly older kids might be better. AKC

animals.name: Milli Vanilli
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Gentle, Chill, Happy

Meet Milli Vanilli! Unlike his namesake, you can be assured there is no lip-synching. When he sings the song of his people, those vocals belong to him!

Milli is a sweet, calm kitty who was recently rescued from the July floods. He is still getting comfortable in his foster home, but has already shown himself to be a kind and loving kitty. We think he is working his way up to cuddles by the way he enjoys getting pets, especially around his ears, and likes to walk near your legs and feet.

Milli is currently being kept in the bathroom of his foster home to give him time to adjust to his new environment one room at a time. This sweet boy cries at night unless a light is kept on in his room. It must be scary being alone in the dark after all he has been through. He is so tidy around the litterbox that he will sweep the floor with his paws to clean up any kitty litter - such a polite gentleman!

Milli’s orange tabby coat has lovely stripes in front and on the top of his head and amazing swirls of cream and orange on his side and back. He is stunning and such a pleasure to pet. The sweetest creamsicle kitty you’ll find!

Milli was initially frightened by the 4-year-old in his foster home. She’s a fast mover, which is a bit much after the upheaval he’s been through. But, he is getting more comfortable around this energetic little human every day.

Milli is a gentle, lovely cat who would be a wonderful addition to a family or person who would enjoy the company of a mellow kitty and who will give him the chance to get comfortable at his own speed. He has a social, easygoing nature which is sure to blossom magnificently with patience, nurturing and time.

If you would like to welcome Milli to your home and give him the love he so richly deserves, contact us for an introduction!

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Milli Vanilli, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org

animals.kennelCardMemo:
Meet your new cuddle buddy! 💙

This sweet boy is the definition of a velcro dog—he loves being close to his people and is happiest when he's by your side. Affectionate, social, and full of love, he greets everyone with the cutest full-body wiggle whenever he's excited. His joyful personality is guaranteed to make you smile.

He rides calmly in the car, walks beautifully on a leash, and is happiest spending time with his favorite humans. He also gets along well with other dogs, taking a little time to get acquainted before becoming fast friends. At home, he's a quiet companion who rarely barks and loves nothing more than curling up for snuggles.

Like any young pup, he's still learning and will benefit from continued training as he grows. He's eager to please and has all the makings of an incredible lifelong companion.

His foster said they would adopt him in a heartbeat—and it's easy to see why. He's the perfect size, has a heart full of love, and is simply looking for a family to call his own. If you're searching for a loyal best friend who wants nothing more than to love and be loved, this handsome boy is ready to meet you. 🐾

memos.Sleepover notes:
He is a lovely boy, and I'm very impressed with him and wanted to share as Madison mentioned fosters should share notes to help find him his forever home so here's what I've got so far along with some pictures.

Collie/Pitbull Mix
He is off to a great start but doesn't seem fully housebroken yet: we had a couple misses at the door and perhaps one marking in the house. Generally, he goes outside but you have to tell him he has to use the potty and take frequent visits especially after drinking water or eating and waking up from naps, he does not signal that HE knows he needs the potty yet.
Very snuggly velcro dog! (typical pitbull) Was my shadow in under 3 hours of handling him. Thinks he's a lap dog. Gets very anxious if you leave the room without him and follows you immediately.
A little nipping (not just mouthing on my hands but nipping on my pants and clothes like a collie), but takes correction to chew toys pretty well, you must repeat but he eventually takes the hint.
Update as of this morning Mon Jul 20, he is nipping excessively and had blown through 2 forever chews/has begun destructive chewing on furniture. Will get more chews but it seems once he gets familiar with the house he is prone to chewing on everything.
This was as of Sunday afternoon - Impressively he has only attempted nibbling on my wicker basket so far. Generally not nibbling on my furniture and redirects to his forever chews pretty well.
Very playful with the toys, has bursts of energy but not an endurance athlete as of yet.
He points/fixates on lizards and birds on walks or in the backyard. He does startle at the TV or gets worked up when you show him Dog TV with birds and squirrels.
I was told he is dog friendly, however I did not test this as he got his little puppy self very worked barking very loud up every time a dog passed by within about 10-12 feet at a dog friendly patio on leash today, he did calm down once the dogs stayed put a good 15-20 feet and was very relaxed but alerted quickly whenever one came near. We took several calm down breaks further away and came back to the people when he relaxed.
UPDATE: Very reactive to dogs 20+ft away, if in sight he whines and barks very loud pulling at the leash and lunging towards the direction of the dogs. He does calm down, and he got better about ignoring dogs behind fences when we tried to run a bit this morning.
Walks - pulls like a typical new pup, once tired out/about 40min of walking he stays to the side of you as coached and is less reactive to passing dogs and bugs/lizards.
Crates himself! - he seems very amenable to two crates I have for him, I'm not sure if he actually understands the command crate but he has comfortably been in both so far, one zipped up for the night in my room with me.
UPDATE: We protested staying in our crate last night. He stays in it well if you're nearby but he'd rather be in your bed or constantly played with or petted.
Keeps jumping on the couch, but we are slowly learning not to do that, especially if we need to 'dig', and we are understanding 'off' slowly.
Loves his kibble, not very patient about waiting for his bowl to be ready once he smells the kibble/hears the bag but we're working on that.
Slowly getting 'sit', starting to learn 'forward' on walks.
Very picky about snacks, didn't seem to like the bag of doggy treats I selected for him.
Pretty good about not begging.
Adorable, sleepy boy, at home and in the car. Very well behaved passenger.
Does NOT like to be left outside alone (closed my glass sliding door to see what he'd do, turns out, sit wait by the door and be a bit sassy when he was let in)
Seems to inherently understand 'fetch' already
LOVES new people, practically melted for my neighbors and rolled over for belly rubs
It is hot out, but given his very short coat and lean frame he still seems a little more sensitive to overheating than I'd expect - throughout today, even relaxed on the patio next to a fan he drank a lot of water and got very hot, he fell asleep as soon as he was in air conditioning. This behavior was the same after our early morning walk today. He took about 3 water breaks/rest in the shade to make it through (about a 2mile walk very good for a pup his age actually)
Seems to have allergies and dry skin (very pitbull like) I washed him off at home in the tub yesterday to get the shelter poo and dirt off him, he did a GREAT job at letting me bathe him although he was a little scared. I notice the bumps I'm seeing are just lumps of dried skin. I'm not sure how to help him with that but if you have a suggestion please let me know.
Not clear on his vocal tendencies - first day he was totally silent. Today we barked at the delivery, the dogs on the walk and at me for not putting the food bowl down fast enough.

Given how velcro and variable his energy is, I'm concerned I'm a fair, but not ideal, home for him as I am a hybrid employee and am commuting from cedar park to downtown/away 3 days a week for 4-7hours each time. I also typically go for very long runs (5-8mile walk/runs about a 2.5 hour trips, home to track to back home), I don't know if that will ever be his thing since he's little, shows promise. I have yet to see how he fairs in his crate alone for a few hours. Seems more prone to have bursts of energy throughout the day and very much is an 'indoor dog'

He is VERY lovable though. I think he will make a great addition to a family with kiddos who intermittently want to play fetch with the dog or someone who is fully remote. He needs constant focus and nearby presence.

animals.name: Beautiful Lady
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Beautiful Lady is a gentle Shepherd mix with a quiet heart and a lot of love to give—once you've earned her trust. She can be shy with new people at first and needs some time to warm up. Once she's comfortable, her tail starts wagging, she seeks out attention, and she'll happily lean into firm head and ear scratches from the people she trusts.

Her favorite place is outside! She loves running and playing chase and would thrive with a securely fenced yard. She's curious and athletic, so she'll need a family that's mindful of open doors and fences while she settles in.

Beautiful Lady is wonderfully quiet. She rarely barks, prefers sleeping on a rug or the floor, and rides nicely in the car. On walks, she's comfortable on a leash but is still learning good leash manners and loves stopping to investigate interesting smells.

Beautiful Lady isn't looking for someone who expects instant affection. She's looking for someone who understands that trust takes time, celebrates the little victories, and knows that the deepest bonds are often the ones that grow slowly. If you're patient, gentle, and willing to let her come to you at her own pace, you'll discover an incredibly loyal companion who quietly fills your life with love.

animals.name: Taco Night
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Calm, Cuddly, Curious

Taco Night likes to crank the affection to max capacity! She loves to be pet, including on her belly. Once she feels safe with you, she will gladly snuggle up for love and attention. When she is not cuddling with you, Taco Night can be found lounging around somewhere or in a cool, dark space where she can hide out. When she emerges from a hiding spot, Taco Night will give a BIGGGG stretch.

Taco Night chirps now and then to say hi, but does not talk much otherwise. She is known for having a super-duper loud purr! Taco Night will purr forever when you pet her.

Taco Night would like a home where she can explore, cuddle, and lounge. She loves a hidey-hole and would likely prefer a lower-energy household. Taco Night has also done well around the resident cat in her foster home; she has been described as neutral and curious.

To quote her foster: “I'd adopt her if I could. You should. Please. Seriously. She's a 10/10 cat.” If that does not convince you to give this sweet girl a chance, I do not know what will.

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Taco Night, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

memos.Behavior Team FFU:
from the sleepover host: We would like to extend our overnight stay for another week. We're not sure if we will be able to foster long term as we're still in the process of introducing him to our other animals. He is a bit higher energy than we expected which is causing some tension. We're working on how to get some of that energy out. When we took him home we discussed getting him fixed as soon as possible and we're hoping that can curb some of his craziness. Please let us know when that can be scheduled.

There are several things we've discovered:
We've only had 3 pee accidents in the house and no poop accidents. Two were on the first day we had him so we think it's just that he wasn't sure how to ask to be let out
He is not aggressive at all: no resource guarding, no aggression towards our other pets, we're able to touch his face, paws, etc. with no concerns. If he oversteps with one of our dogs and gets a corrective growl, he will flop over and show his belly. Very submissive
He hardly barks
He is not crate trained but we are working on it. He is fine when he is in the crate (no barking or whining or trying to get out) but we have to physically put him in the crate
He is incredibly smart. We've already been able to teach him "sit", "lay down", and "touch" (putting his nose to our palm). He's almost mastered "up" as well. We're still working on "paw" and "in a circle."
He only likes chicken flavoured treats
The only time he tries to get onto furniture is if someone is on it and wants to get on their lap
His favorite toys are squeaky toys and the flirt. He is not interested in tug of war at all and is only mildly into fetch but only the throw part and not the giving back part
He is a very very sweet boy

Now for the bad news:
Paul has not been properly socialized with other dogs. While he is eager to please and wants to play, he gets in other dogs' faces which upsets them
He is not leash trained and lunges at other dogs (he wants to play with, not harm them but sounds aggressive). We are working on it but we can't get his energy out with long walks because they are slow going with the training. It's also a million degrees out so we only have limited windows to try
He has puppy problems
He's destroyed a pillow, a dog bed, and chewed up part of the carpet (he only does these bad things when I'm on meetings and can't catch him in the act 😭)
He's constantly getting in our other pets faces to the point where our gentle "loves all creatures and wants to be friends with them" dog doesn't want to interact with him
Jumping and nipping are big problems. Because he's so big, the nipping legitimately hurts. We're doing our best to discourage the behaviours but these are our biggest problems
We know that those issues are typical for puppies but him being 70lbs means that the impact of those behaviors is greater. We also know that giving him an outlet for that energy will help so we're trying to figure out how best to do that. Learning tricks helps and we have high hopes for the flirt which we've just introduced. Again, we think that getting him fixed will help so please let us know how soon that can be scheduled.
sent resources addressing issues.

animals.name: Eclipse
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Meet Eclipse: Your Future Furry Friend! 🌟

Eclipse is a delightful medium-sized poodle with a heart full of love and a tail that never stops wagging! This super friendly girl is always ready to greet everyone she meets with enthusiasm, making her the perfect companion for anyone looking for a little extra joy in their life.

Personality

• Energetic and Playful: Eclipse loves her daily adventures and thrives on plenty of walks. She’s eager to explore, sniff around, and meet new friends along the way.

• Cuddle Bug: After a good romp, this sweet girl is more than happy to curl up on the couch for some cozy snuggles.

Training and Manners

• House-Trained: Eclipse has mastered her potty training and is quick to do her business outside.

• Basic Commands: She already knows “sit” and “shake,” showcasing her intelligence and eagerness to learn.

• Room for Improvement: While she’s a fast learner, Eclipse will benefit from some additional training to curb her enthusiasm for placing her paws on counters and people.

Ideal Home

Eclipse would thrive in an active household where she can get the exercise she needs and plenty of love. Whether you’re an individual or a family, she’s ready to bring joy and companionship into your life.

If you’re looking for a smart, friendly, and playful pup to brighten your days, Eclipse is the one for you! Come meet her and see if you can resist those adorable tail wags!

This sweet boy is looking for a family that will enjoy teaching him new things, celebrating his progress, and sharing plenty of snacks along the way. With patience, kindness, and lots of positive reinforcement, he's sure to blossom into an incredible lifelong companion. 💙

animals.kennelCardMemo:
Hi, I'm Mouse Knight! I recently found my way to Austin, a city full of new smells and sights. After a big change in my life, I'm now at this cozy shelter, making friends and waiting for someone like you to take me home. If you're looking for a dog who loves everyone they meet, this happy pup checks every box. Friendly, affectionate, and always wearing a smile, they have a joyful personality that makes every day a little brighter. Whether it's going for a walk, exploring the outdoors, playing, or curling up for cuddle time, they're happiest simply being with their people.

This sweet dog is house-trained, walks beautifully on a leash, and gets along wonderfully with both people and other dogs. They're eager to please, well-mannered, and always ready for the next adventure,or the next snuggle on the couch.

When it's time to relax, you'll find them happily enjoying a bone, a peanut butter treat, or dinner with a little water mixed into their kibble. Their loving nature and easygoing personality make them a wonderful companion for all kinds of families.

With a heart full of love and a tail that never stops wagging, this amazing pup is ready to find the forever home they deserve

memos.Disclaimer:
The dog you are adopting or fostering has been rescued from one of our more under-resourced partner shelters and unfortunately has come to us with ticks on them. Rest assured that upon their arrival they were treated with Nexgard which will kill fleas within hours and the ticks within 24-48 hours. Often the dead tick will detach on its own, but not always and might require removal.

We understand that this can be concerning to bring into your home, but we have some ideas that have worked for other fosters and adopters previously. In order to limit the spreading of the ticks while they are dying we recommend keeping the dog in a spare bathroom, bedroom or a x-pen area for this initial period. This will help with clean-up if they are in a smaller space where it is easier to clean up afterwards. Additionally, baths can help with removing the ticks! Just be aware that after the first bath you’ll want to use water only so you aren’t stripping your dog’s coat of their naturally occurring oils which could make them itchy.

If you have any concerns about your resident dog getting ticks from your foster or adopted dog, please let us know and we can provide a single dose of tick meds for them as well while your new APA! dog is getting rid of their ticks.

memos.Volunteer Notes:
How long was your Sleepover
6 days

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Affectionate
Calm

Cheerful

Low-maintenance
Obedient
Smart
Trusting
Velcro Dog
Well-Trained

What made you smile or laugh about them?
She smiles when she is happy. She is a big ol goofy lap dog. She loves to attack sprinklers

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
SHE IS AMAZING!!!!! Potty trained, not a single accident in the house in six days. She is kennel trained and sleeps in there all night without concern. She knows basic commands like sit and shake and sometimes lay down.

The only time she tries to go out the front door is if I am going out but stops and stays when I tell her to. She has not barked in the house but will bark at people talking on the other side of the fence, although it is not often. She seems fascinated by squirrels.

She does not have separation anxiety or bark when the garage door opens. She is not motivated by food or treats but will take one when I give my dog one. She does not want to eat just kibble so I mix in a tiny bit of gravy and she scarfs it down. She doesn't really beg for food when I am eating and if she gets too close I tell her no and she goes and lays down. I have been calling her Piper and she is starting to respond to it.

She is very easily redirected and listens to no and stop. Her one bad habit, which mostly is because I am not used to it, is that she paws at you when she wants to be pet. As soon as you pet her, she stops, but as soon as you stop, she starts pawing again. It is very gentle and I am trying to break her of this habit.

While she does follow me everywhere I go, she does not necessarily need attention, she just wants to be in the same room. If I am on the couch, she waits for permission but does get on it on her own when no one else is on it. My favorite silly thing about her is that she LOVES sprinklers and will beeline right to it and put her whole mouth on the small ones and chomps at the water from the bigger one. She walks well on a leash, unless she sees a sprinkler and then pulls (not too hard) to get to it.

Crate

Relaxed

Relaxed

Fully housetrained - Consistently holds it when left alone, and gives clear signals when they need to go outside. May have had accidents in the first couple days, but leveled out completely once the dog learned the routines.

Did not attempt to give the dog a bath

Loved everyone

Not applicable

Great!

animals.name: Katie Katwalk
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Gorgeous, Loving, People-oriented

Katie Katwalk is ready to walk her way right into your heart! This sweet girl always wants to be right where you are and loves connecting with her people. Whether that’s simply hanging out in the same room as you or reaching out with a gentle paw to touch your face, Katie Katwalk wants you to know she’s happy to be near you.

Katie Katwalk came to Austin Pets Alive! from Uvalde following the floods, and she’s shown what a resilient and loving kitty she truly is. She still has lots of kitten energy and gets the zoomies often, and you’ll catch her playing with the most random items she can find! But once playtime is over, Katie Katwalk is ready for cuddles, rubbing against your legs and making endless biscuits. She has a soft voice and only meows on occasion.

In her foster home, Katie Katwalk has shown a gentle, easygoing nature around other cats. While she can be a little shy at first, she warms up at her own pace and enjoys lounging on the bed alongside her feline foster friends. Because of her more reserved nature, she would do best in a quieter home without rowdy dogs or kids. Otherwise, her affectionate, snuggly demeanor makes her a wonderful fit for almost any family looking for the sweetest kitty friend!

All APA! cats are fully vetted, spayed or neutered, and have updated vaccines and a microchip. Lifetime support is offered by our Cat Behavior Team.

For further information or to meet Katie Katwalk, please email adopt@austinpetsalive.org.

memos.Disclaimer:
"Flight Risk" is a term used to describe when dogs who may have a strong tendency to escape or run away when they feel scared, anxious, bored, or overstimulated. This behavior can be triggered by loud noises, unfamiliar environments, lack of engagement, something desirable, or even a sudden movement. While dogs are transitioning into a new environment or home, there is a higher likelihood to see escape attempts.

Specific Behavior:

Strategies for Managing and Supporting Dogs who Present a Flight Risk
- Secure Environment: Ensure that your home and yard are escape-proof. This means checking fences for any gaps or weaknesses, making sure gates latch securely, and being mindful of any potential escape routes. Consider adding additional barriers, like baby gates or temporary fencing, to further secure the area.
- Leash and Tethering: Keep a drag leash clipped to your dog’s collar for at least the first month while your dog is acclimating to their new home. When outside, always keep your dog on a leash, even in a fenced yard, until you are confident in their ability to stay within the boundaries. Do not leave them unattended when outside. A double-leash system (using both a harness and a collar) can provide extra security during walks, and a martingale collar will prevent him from being able to slip out and away. Avoid using a retractable leash, as they can easily break.
- Safe Entry and Exit: Be cautious when opening doors, as many flight-risk dogs may seize any opportunity to dart outside. Teach your dog to wait calmly before doors are opened, and set up gates or other air lock systems around exterior doors and gates to prevent door darting. When going on car rides, tether his leash outside of the door to ensure you can get a firm hold on it before opening the door. Do not leave windows open in the car during car rides, and never allow him to be off-leash in public.
- Identification & Tracking: Ensure your dog is always wearing a collar with up-to-date identification tags. Microchipping is also highly recommended as an additional layer of security, as well as attaching an Apple Airtag to their collar.
- Training and Positive Reinforcement: Work on building a strong recall response within him where he will reliably return to you when prompted.

Snow White pup 1 presents for DVM evaluation
Foster reports- was Lethargic overnight, increased RR. 
2 d ago noticed more gargly noises w/ breathing and coughing, started on azithromycin for potential aspiration
Last night episode of open mouth breathing, panting, lethargy, did fading puppy protocol w/ tech overnight, has perked up, e is back but still not wanting to nurse on mom, offered bottle didnt take it, weight stagnant, no v/d other concerns. Other puppies are doing great

physicalExams.plan:
BG 137
DV radiograph taken due to wiggly puppy- difficult to interpret due to positioning etc, does look suspicious/concerning for pneumonia forming, some patchy infiltrates + in some areas alveolar pattern seen partially superimposed over heart and in caudodorsal lung fields
Tech offered bottle-no interest
Pulse ox 100% on room air
Continue w/ current meds, nebulize before feedings if nebulizer available (vs humidifier or steam therapy)
If still fighting nursing and bottle feeding, tube feed if foster comfortable
Give "goodies" package today with 12 ml LRS SQ, 0.07 ml of Cerenia, Famotidine and Ondansetron, 0.05 ml of Vitamin B12 SQ
Rx LRS 12 ml SQ BID x 72 total (so next dose due tonight, then for 2 additional days), so 5 doses total
Rx Cerenia (10 mg/ml) 0.07 ml SQ SID x 2 d (starting tomorrow AM)
Rx Baytril (20 mg/ml) 0.3 ml PO SIDx 14d (*tech called and added this med on after visit, initially thought puppy was on amoxicillin so wanted to switch to amoxiclav, later found out was actually on azithromycin, so adding in baytril for broader spectrum coverage given radiographic findings
Request update in 48h on how doing, if declining sooner let us know

animals.name: Shadow Horse
animals.kennelCardMemo:
Meet a handsome 3-year-old German Shepherd who brings together everything people love about the breed: intelligence, loyalty, playful energy, and a huge heart. He enjoys meeting new people and is always ready to make a new friend, especially when cuddles might be involved.

In his foster home, he has been fully house trained and gets along well with other dogs. He is also remarkably quiet—his foster has yet to hear him bark! He settles nicely into a home routine and has shown that he can be an easy, enjoyable companion.

This playful guy loves long walks and would be thrilled to join someone who enjoys exploring the neighborhood or heading out on daily adventures. Exercise helps him burn off his youthful energy, and once he has had a good walk, he is perfectly content to relax and recharge.

One of his favorite pastimes is lounging by a window and watching the world go by. Whether he is observing people, cars, or neighborhood activity, he is happy to take it all in from his favorite viewing spot before settling in for a nap.

Most of all, he is a complete cuddle fanatic. He does not simply sit beside you—he leans his whole body in, wraps his paws around you like a hug, and gazes up with the sweetest, most loving expression. His goofy, enthusiastic way of showing affection is impossible to resist, and he is ready to give one lucky family all the hugs they can handle.

New to the APA! family during the 2026 flood relief, Wheat Thin came from a small shelter ahead of the heavy rains. Luckily a new foster family came to his resuce and give him a chance in a home (maybe the first time he's EVER been in a home!)

Wheat Thin has shown that he LOVES people. LOVES. THEM. He's such a people pleaser and wants to show every person he's met how good he can be. memos.Disclaimer:
"Flight Risk" is a term used to describe when dogs who may have a strong tendency to escape or run away when they feel scared, anxious, bored, or overstimulated. This behavior can be triggered by loud noises, unfamiliar environments, lack of engagement, something desirable, or even a sudden movement. While dogs are transitioning into a new environment or home, there is a higher likelihood to see escape attempts.

Specific Behavior: Sleepover host noted that he pulled hard on leash in reaction to loud noises. Additionally the host noted that escaped a wire crate.

Strategies for Managing and Supporting Dogs who Present a Flight Risk
- Secure Environment: Ensure that your home and yard are escape-proof. This means checking fences for any gaps or weaknesses, making sure gates latch securely, and being mindful of any potential escape routes. Consider adding additional barriers, like baby gates or temporary fencing, to further secure the area.
- Leash and Tethering: Keep a drag leash clipped to your dog’s collar for at least the first month while your dog is acclimating to their new home. When outside, always keep your dog on a leash, even in a fenced yard, until you are confident in their ability to stay within the boundaries. Do not leave them unattended when outside. A double-leash system (using both a harness and a collar) can provide extra security during walks, and a martingale collar will prevent him from being able to slip out and away. Avoid using a retractable leash, as they can easily break.
- Safe Entry and Exit: Be cautious when opening doors, as many flight-risk dogs may seize any opportunity to dart outside. Teach your dog to wait calmly before doors are opened, and set up gates or other air lock systems around exterior doors and gates to prevent door darting. When going on car rides, tether his leash outside of the door to ensure you can get a firm hold on it before opening the door. Do not leave windows open in the car during car rides, and never allow him to be off-leash in public.
- Identification & Tracking: Ensure your dog is always wearing a collar with up-to-date identification tags. Microchipping is also highly recommended as an additional layer of security, as well as attaching an Apple Airtag to their collar.
- Training and Positive Reinforcement: Work on building a strong recall response within him where he will reliably return to you when prompted.

Last Updated: 7/26/26 Initials: TH

The only issue I am having is the kennel. I work overnights and my husband works day shift. So there is about 30 mins twice a day when he needs to be in the kennel. We had practiced going in and out of the kennel with treats as a reward. Then I would set up my camera and leave for 10 mins and come back. He did show some anxiety but I didn’t see him trying to get out. The kennel I had was a wire kennel and he ripped the wire from the side and forced the door open; by the time I got home he was out of the kennel definitely panicked. I looked him over and he didn’t hurt himself. No scratches and his teeth and gums looked good. No bleeding. I have then tried to leave him out of the kennel and just roam free but that seemed to make things worse he was jumping onto ledges and counters so I was scared he would fall and hurt himself.

memos.Volunteer Notes:
How long was your Sleepover
4 nights

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Affectionate
Eager-to-please
Chill
Curious
Low-maintenance
Silly
Trusting
Watchful

What made you smile or laugh about them?
Goofyness. His love of toys.

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
He was scared of stairs, at least the outdoor cement ones. But with some coaxing he made it up. By the end of day 2 he had mastered the stairs!

Did good with a bath, will try to jump out but if you let him keep his head in your lap he'll mostly listen. He likes to try and sneakily step out but it helps if you you pull the shower curtain on the tub and he can't see out.

Physical touch is his love language. He wants to lay with you/ on you on the couch, he likes to be up against you! If he whines while you drive reaching a hand back calms him down (again, physical touch!). If he determines you've been on your phone too long, he'll scoot closer and try to capture attention with head nudges.

He actively watches TV, he paid particular attention to cowboys versus aliens.

Has very minor separation anxiety, and it doesn't last long. If you close a room door or walk out the front, he'll whine for a few minutes but then he goes and sits somewhere to wait for you.
*He was loose and alone on Saturday for 2 hours and laid at the door waiting. He was loose and alone today while I'm working and is still just laying at the door (approx 7 hours). Zero destructive behavior.

He's respectful of furniture, he'll let you know he wants to come up but if you tell him no and set his paws back down on the ground and respects that he's not allowed to come up. He was told no once for the bed and didn't try again. I invited/allowed him on the couch and he happily joined to snuggle!

He really likes giving kisses, but prefers if you take it slower on giving him some back!

He loves toys! Especially ones that squeak, he likes for you to throw it and then he'll bring it back to play tug of war with a playful growl and tail wagging. He does not know the drop command.

He's a good leash-walker, he doesn't pull. He walks in front of and beside you but doesn't pull on the leash at all.

Friendly with other dogs, likes to play. He does do some nose-nudges to other dogs which can sometimes annoy them.

He hasn't fully figured out mirrors or reflections in windows, and is very curious about the 'other dog' looking at him! He's a silly guy.

Negative: He's a big licker, and also tries to hump (both myself and another male dog he met).

Dog Bed

How was the dog in the car?
Some whining or pacing, but settled

How was the dog when left alone?
Some whining or pacing
Relaxed

Fully housetrained - Consistently holds it when left alone, and gives clear signals when they need to go outside. May have had accidents in the first couple days, but leveled out completely once the dog learned the routines.

Tolerant

Warmed up over time

Not applicable

No children present

Loved them

Moderate

Mostly loose leash
Great!

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
If I was in the market to adopt a dog, I would consider him. But at the moment I am not ready to have a full time dog. My dogs passed last year and I am not ready to fully adopt.

Tony the Tiger suffered a severe bite injury to his head that caused suspected skull fractures, infected wounds/abscesses, and loss of his left eye. Despite these serious injuries, he was alert, walking normally, and otherwise stable at his exam; he will remain permanently blind on the left side, and his longer-term prognosis depends on how well the infection and skull injuries heal. Tony is receiving doxycycline for infection, carprofen for pain and inflammation, and gabapentin for pain; medications are currently prescribed through July 31, 2026, and no refills are documented, so they should be given exactly as labeled. He is scheduled for a sedated clinic appointment on July 22, 2026, to thoroughly clean the wounds and possibly surgically close the empty left eye socket, with additional follow-up based on those findings.

Please see the medical record for the complete medical history. This is only a synopsis of the most important information.

memos.Volunteer Notes:
How long was your Sleepover
9 days

Select at least three traits that best describe this dog:
Affectionate
Velcro Dog
Silly
Fun-loving
Cheerful

What made you smile or laugh about them?
Everything! This dog is pure joy. He is goofy and clumsy, will do anything to get close to you including tumbling over himself before curling up in the crook of your arm. His underbite causes his bottom teeth to stick out, which gives him the funniest expressions, and when he listens intently his right ear perks straight up while his left ear stays folded. There is nothing cuter! He recently felt confident and comfortable enough to show off some zoomies in our backyard, and that was pure joy to watch!

Is there anything a future adopter should know to set them up for success?
Limo has the sweetest soul and aims to please! He has been so tolerant of baths, car rides, crate training (primarily at night, he's learning to be brave in there alone during the day), sharing toys, and getting on potty break schedules. That said, he's still young and is learning how to be a proper gentleman! It will take no time at all to teach him basic commands and how to be a good citizen on a leash. He can still be a little bit nervous on walks but is growing more confident by the minute as he settles in. He will do everything in his power to be a good boy! He is phenomenal at going potty out in our backyard, but gets distracted on walks - so, if you're wanting to make sure that he has gone potty before heading out of the house or letting him roam free, I would recommend taking him to a yard or designated grass patch that he gets used to when getting started.

Where did the dog sleep
Crate

How was the dog in the car?
Some whining or pacing, but settled

How was the dog when left alone?
Some whining or pacing

What is their housetraining status?
Mostly housetrained - Understands the concept and thrives on a routine, but may have occasional accidents if left alone for too long, during transitions, or when excited. May have 1-2 accidents per week.

How did the dog do in the bath?
Had fun and loved it!

How did they do with other adults in the home or visitors? Did they meet visitors, or only hang with you?
Loved everyone

How did they do with cats or small animals (if present)?
Not applicable

How did they do with children (if present)?
No children present

How did they do with other dogs (if present)?
Loved them

If you select 'Not Recommended" to any of the answers above. Please use this space to tell us why you choice that selection.

How would you describe their energy level?
Moderate

How were they on leash?
Pulled sometimes

Do you want to add any details about the information you provided above?

Would you adopt this dog if you could? Why or why not?
I would adopt this dog in a heartbeat if I could! I will be heartbroken to say goodbye to him, but will be so excited for his future family to hit the jackpot with him! He is a joy to be around and makes me laugh all the time. He has shown unconditional love every second that we have had him, and is the best cuddler I've ever met! He doesn't bark, is so gentle and friendly with dogs (he has been very respectful of our small resident dogs, who are 6 and 13) and people. He is honestly a dream!
